title: Private release serializer and idempotent batch applier for zero-drift upgrades
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: We need a deterministic release serialization layer plus an idempotent batch applier for Redwood Private upgrades. Goal: enable zero-drift staged upgrades across VPC/on-prem cohorts by serializing intent (release units) and applying them in repeatable, resumable batches with conflict detection and automated repair hooks. This ticket covers design + PoC implementation of the serializer, the applier worker, preflight invariant checks, and the lightweight quiesce/health hooks required to avoid split-brain during stateful schema migrations. This is targeted for private-2026.04 and must integrate with existing rollout policy config in the Console and Dedicated rollout scheduling API.
comments: 2026-02-15 — initial writeup: sketched 'release unit' protobuf that bundles: artifact version, DB migration plan id, KV-state preimage hash, cohort selector, gating predicates. Decided to keep serializer format small and signable to support out-of-band audit and rollbacks.

2026-02-22 — architecture sync: chose a push-pull model where central controller writes serialized release units to S3-like storage and per-customer applier pulls and applies idempotent steps. Trade-off: simpler central orchestration vs. more network hops. Team prefers push-pull to reduce blast radius and allow offline private environments to fetch when allowed.

2026-03-01 — engineering design review: Jonas suggested embedding a 'preflight manifest' with lightweight checks (disk space, node versions, kernel params) and a deterministic dry-run verifier. PM requested clear signal semantics for 'soft-fail' vs 'hard-fail' in preflight.

2026-03-05 — prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrades/pull/347 — implements serializer service and applier worker with optimistic apply and per-step idempotency tokens. Initial unit tests for restart/resume paths added. Requesting review from infra and security.

2026-03-10 — security review notes: ensure release unit signatures are verified before applying; KMS integration design documented. Also flagged need to encrypt bundle metadata at rest for on-prem tenants — follow-up task created.

2026-03-12 — testing update: ran end-to-end in lab cluster (vpc-sim-3). Observed race when two appliers attempted to claim same cohort during forced requeue; added lightweight lease via DB row and reworked exponential backoff. Resolved flaky rollback detection by increasing telemetry window.

2026-03-14 — PM feedback: include a Console toggle to require 'manual approval' for any release units that include schema-altering migrations. Added UI story to the private upgraders roadmap. Next: formalize acceptance criteria and complete integration tests against on-prem snapshot harness.
acceptance_criteria: Serializer emits immutable, signed release unit bundles; verifier rejects unsigned/altered bundles.
Applier worker can apply a release unit in idempotent steps and resume cleanly after process restart without double-applying side effects.
Preflight manifest checks surface soft/hard failures in the Console and block rollout when hard failures are present.
A demo rollout executes across a 5-customer cohort in lab with zero data-drift and an automated abort+safe-rollback path exercised.
KMS integration design validated and security sign-off obtained (security_review_required = true).
Integration tests covering concurrent applier claim contention and lease recovery pass consistently in CI for 20 runs.
